How ratings develop with age

Average year-over-year rating change, by age — batters
Ratings almost never decline before age 30 in this engine; decline sets in around 31–32. Contact (CH) and Control (CO) develop hardest and finish by ~26; Power (PH) and HR-avoidance keep growing into the late 20s.

Click a row for the full player page. *Players 27+ show current predicted value (small type) instead of a prime projection.

Method & accuracy

Panel: 71,014 batter-seasons (5,012 careers) and 48,636 pitcher-seasons (3,357 careers), linked by name + age progression with ratings tie-breaking. Projection = k-nearest-neighbor comps (same age, similar ratings and similar recent growth — growth speed is persistent, r≈0.53) blended per-rating with the mean aging curve; band is the comps’ 10th–90th percentile prime outcome. Backtest (held-out players, project from age 22 to prime): CH ±7.2, PH ±7.3, FA ±8.2, SP ±4.5, AS ±2.7 for batters; CO ±6.8, best pitch ±3.6, 2nd pitch ±3.8, EN ±2.6, AS ±1.7 for pitchers (mean absolute error, 0–99 scale). Pitcher list is ranked by predicted prime ERA; batter list by predicted prime OPS. Stat models fit on 15,049 pitcher-seasons and 16,498 batter-seasons (300+ AB / 60+ IP): best pitch is the strongest ERA driver, ahead of control; Hold Runners has no ERA effect; contact and power drive nearly all of OPS. Typical model error: ±.022 AVG, ±.042 SLG, ±4.8 HR, ±0.5 ERA. Current snapshot: January 6, 2076 (offseason). Its part-year growth is scaled to full-year equivalents for comps matching.
